title: null and nullable values (missing data for structs)
hook: Reference types like `string` can be `null` when there is no object. Value types like `int` cannot — unless you wrap them in `int?`, which means "maybe an int, maybe nothing."

blocks.text: `null` means "no object" for reference types. An `int` sitting in a variable always holds a number — it cannot be empty. To represent a missing integer (for example, a Redis cache entry with no Time To Live (TTL)), C# provides **nullable value types**: `int?` is shorthand for `Nullable<int>`, a small struct with `HasValue` (true/false) and `Value` (the `int` when present). This is different from **nullable reference types** (`string?`), which is a compiler annotation covered in module 07 — at run time `string?` is still just `string`.

entries.plainDefinition: A special value for reference types meaning "points to no object." It is not zero, not false, and not JavaScript `undefined`.
entries.example: `string? token = null;` — no string object exists.

entries.plainDefinition: A struct wrapper that adds a "has a value" flag to any value type. Written as `T?` in C#.
entries.example: `int? ttl = null;` — no TTL was found in cache.

entries.plainDefinition: Returns the left side if it has a value; otherwise returns the right side. Works for both reference null and nullable value types.
entries.example: `int ttl = ttlSeconds ?? 60;` — use 60 when TTL is missing.

blocks.text: Using `0` to mean "missing" collides with a real zero. A Redis key with TTL `0` might mean "expire immediately," while a missing key is a different story. `int?` lets you model three states: has value, no value, and you never confuse them with `0`. For strings, `null` means no object — but module 07 will teach you how the compiler warns when you forget to check.

blocks.title: Two different "nullable" stories
blocks.body: `int?` is a real different run-time type (`Nullable<int>` struct). `string?` in a nullable-enabled project is the same `string` type with a compiler warning overlay — that is module 07, not this page.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Declare a nullable value type
items.body: `int? ttlSeconds = null;` creates a `Nullable<int>` with `HasValue == false`.

items.title: Check before reading .Value
items.body: Calling `.Value` when `HasValue` is false throws `InvalidOperationException`. Prefer `if (ttl is int seconds)` or `ttl ?? 60`.

items.title: Use lifted operators
items.body: `ttl + 1` returns `int?` — if `ttl` is null, the result is null. No exception.

items.title: Distinguish from reference null
items.body: `string? token = null` is a reference with no object. `int? count = null` is a struct reporting "no value." Different mechanisms, same `??` and `?.` syntax in many cases.

diagram.title: int? vs string null

snippet.label: Nullable value vs reference null
snippet.explanation: Line 1: `int?` is a struct wrapper, not a reference. Line 2: `string?` is still a reference type (annotation only until module 07). Line 6: `??` picks 60 when `ttlSeconds` has no value.

snippet.label: Safe extraction with patterns
snippet.explanation: Line 3: pattern `is { } seconds` checks `HasValue` and extracts the `int`. Line 8: `GetValueOrDefault(30)` returns 30 when missing. Line 11: `.Value` without a check throws — a common interview trap.

snippet.label: Lifted operators on int?
snippet.explanation: Line 4: nullable arithmetic is "lifted" — if any operand is missing, the result is missing (null), not an exception. Line 8–9: both `HasValue` and `is null` work for checking nullable value types.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Calling `.Value` on `int?` without checking `HasValue` — throws `InvalidOperationException`. Storing cache misses as `0` instead of `int?` and colliding with a real zero TTL. Confusing `string?` (reference annotation, module 07) with `int?` (a different run-time struct type).

interviewTakeaways: `T?` on a value type is `Nullable<T>` — a different struct at run time.
`T?` on a reference type (nullable reference types) is the same CLR type with annotations — module 07.
commonPitfalls: Using `== null` on a `Nullable<T>` when `is null` / pattern is clearer, but both work.
Storing Redis misses as `0` instead of `int?` and colliding with a real zero TTL.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript has both `null` and `undefined`. C# locals cannot be unread; optional values are `null` (references) or `T?` (value types). There is no separate `undefined`.
`number | null` is a union erased at run time. `int?` is a real `Nullable<int>` wrapper struct. `string | null` is closer to annotated `string?`.
